summary: 1941 Aermotor MC-39 fire tower near Jasper, Walker County, Alabama; dedicated June 18, 1941; NHLR-registered 2023 and on private property. No staffing or fire sources found.

access.note: NHLR says the tower is located on private property; no owner or permission information found

events.note: Completed by May 29, 1941 per a 1941 newspaper report quoted on Forest Lookouts; dedicated June 18, 1941. NHLR lists the build year as unknown.
Registered July 24, 2023 as US 1745, AL 83; nominated by Jason Johns

evidence.quote: This tower is a 100ft Aermotor MC-39.

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
tower lies just southwest of Jasper
State Department of Conservation planned a wooden tower
evidence.quote: announced a wooden fire tower would be erected at this place

evidence.supports: friends offered to pay the difference for an all-steel structure
evidence.quote: contribute the difference in the cost of the proposed wooden tower and an all-steel structure
The plan was cordially approved by the officials of the Department

evidence.supports: all-steel tower complete in the May 29, 1941 report

evidence.quote: the all-steel tower is now completed
dedicated Wednesday afternoon, June 18, in the presence of about 700 people

evidence.supports: tablet honors Aldridge's work on conservation in Alabama
evidence.quote: his effective work in the cause of conservation of natural resources in Alabama

evidence.supports: Walker County; the 1941 report says the honoree had done much for Walker County
friends of the late Abner B. Aldridge proposed the naming and the all-steel structure
evidence.quote: friends of the late Abner B. Aldridge

evidence.supports: stone tablet erected at the base of the tower
evidence.quote: large stone tablet erected at the base of the Aldridge fire tower
dedicated to the memory of Abner Bell Aldridge

evidence.supports: many historic lookouts unsafe and illegal to climb
evidence.quote: Many are looking worse for the wear, are very unsafe, and are illegal to climb.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: The 1941 history comes from newspaper passages quoted on the Forest Lookouts page (Daily Mountain Eagle), not from the original paper. The Weebly passage spells it 'Alridge Tower'; the tablet and NHLR use Aldridge. NHLR lists the build year as unknown, so the 1941 event rests on the May 29, 1941 'now completed' line and the June 1941 dedication. Brief gap closed: no built event was in the record. Access upgraded from unknown to private from NHLR's 'located on private property' line; no owner or permission information was found. Not verified: condition after the July 2022 site visit, staffing and fires. Kaufmann's column is general and does not name this tower. No photos added.
